blocks.md: Moving window functions (msfunc/minvfunc) enable O(1) sliding window instead of O(k) recompute. Critical for high-frequency streaming aggregates. Must be implemented in C for performance.

items.explain: msfunc adds new value, minvfunc removes old value — O(1) per slide vs O(k) recompute.
State transition functions must be IMMUTABLE and fast. C implementation required for msfunc/minvfunc performance.

blocks.label: hypothetical rank
blocks.code:
-- Rank of hypothetical value 100000 in salary distribution
SELECT 
  RANK(100000) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS rank_of_100k,
  DENSE_RANK(100000) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS dense_rank_of_100k,
  PERCENT_RANK(100000) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS pct_rank_of_100k
FROM employees;

-- Multiple hypothetical values
SELECT 
  RANK(50000) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS rank_50k,
  RANK(100000) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS rank_100k,
  RANK(200000) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) AS rank_200k
FROM employees;

blocks.label: ignore nulls
blocks.code:
-- LAG/LEAD with IGNORE NULLS
SELECT 
  sale_date,
  amount,
  LAG(amount) IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS prev_non_null,
  LEAD(amount) IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS next_non_null
FROM daily_sales;

-- FIRST_VALUE / LAST_VALUE with IGNORE NULLS
SELECT 
  sale_date,
  amount,
  FIRST_VALUE(amount) IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS first_sale,
  LAST_VALUE(amount) IGNORE NULLS OVER (
    ORDER BY sale_date
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  ) AS last_sale
FROM daily_sales;

-- RESPECT NULLS (default)
LAG(amount) RESPECT NULLS OVER (ORDER BY sale_date)
blocks.py-pandas:
# Forward/backward fill
df['amount'].ffill()  # forward fill (LAG IGNORE NULLS)
df['amount'].bfill()  # backward fill (LEAD IGNORE NULLS)

items.explain: IGNORE NULLS skips NULLs and finds previous non-NULL value.

items.explain: Default frame = CURRENT ROW. Need explicit frame for true last non-NULL.

sections.title: Window Function Internals — WindowAgg, Sort, Spilling

blocks.md: PostgreSQL WindowAgg node: 1) Sort input by PARTITION BY + ORDER BY, 2) For each partition, evaluate window functions in sequence, 3) For each row, compute frame boundaries and evaluate functions. Multiple functions with same PARTITION+ORDER share sort and single WindowAgg pass.

blocks.label: windowagg internals
blocks.code:
-- EXPLAIN shows WindowAgg node
EXPLAIN SELECT 
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary),
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary),
  SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary)
FROM employees;

-- Single WindowAgg node with multiple functions
-- Plan shows:
--   -> WindowAgg
--       -> Sort (partition by dept, order by salary)
--             -> Seq Scan on employees
blocks.pg:
-- Single WindowAgg for same PARTITION+ORDER
-- Different PARTITION/ORDER = multiple WindowAgg nodes
blocks.py-pandas: # No direct equivalent; pandas uses groupby + transform

items.q: Two window functions: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary) and SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary). Execution:
items.explain: Same PARTITION+ORDER = shared sort. Each function = separate WindowAgg pass over sorted data.

options: Computed on-the-fly per row during WindowAgg pass
items.explain: WindowAgg iterates rows, computes frame boundaries per row, evaluates aggregate over frame.

blocks.sql: SUM(x) OVER (PARTITION BY y ORDER BY z RANGE BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING)
blocks.pg: Full RANGE frame support with numeric/date ORDER BY
blocks.mysql: MySQL 8.0+: RANGE supported for numeric/date. No GROUPS frame.

blocks.sql: SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary) FROM emp QUALIFY rn <= 3;
blocks.pg:
-- QUALIFY not in PostgreSQL
-- Use CTE: WITH cte AS (...) SELECT * FROM cte WHERE rn <= 3
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: QUALIFY supported
SELECT ... FROM emp QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary) <= 3;

-- FOR EACH ROW vs FOR EACH STATEMENT;
-- BEFORE can mutate NEW; AFTER can't change rows

-- CREATE TRIGGER ... BEFORE INSERT ON t FOR EACH ROW
-- only one trigger per timing/event/table, OLD/NEW row

# pandas has no triggers; application-layer hooks

blocks.label: instead of trigger
blocks.pg:
-- INSTEAD OF triggers exist only on views (not tables)
-- keep the view INSIDE the trigger simply and idempotent
blocks.mysql: -- INSTEAD OF works on views in MySQL too
blocks.py-pandas:
# view writes stay a DB concept; pandas reads views,

blocks.md: **Triggers are invisible to EXPLAIN's node tree** — the plan shows the driving DML only. Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE's trailing `Triggers:` section to time them, and keep trigger bodies thin: they run inside the transaction and every row waits on them.

items.q: INSTEAD OF triggers can only be created on:
items.explain: INSTEAD OF is the view-writability mechanism; tables get BEFORE/AFTER row triggers.

items.q: RAISE EXCEPTION inside a BEFORE trigger:
options: Aborts the statement and rolls back the transaction
items.explain: An uncaught exception aborts the transaction — the standard way to enforce invariants beyond FK constraints.
